title: Find a value, change it, find what writes it
summary: Find a number the game shows (health, ammo, money) in its memory, change or freeze it, and find the instruction that writes it: the place a lasting patch changes.

steps.title: Open Cheat Engine on the game
steps.text: In RUNTIME, DEBUGGER AND MEMORY: LIST TARGETS, then CONTINUE IN CHEAT ENGINE, and start the game. ViWo's table attaches to the game's process as soon as it runs.
steps.expect: The top of Cheat Engine names the game's process.

steps.title: First scan
steps.text: In the game, pick a number you can change and note it. In Cheat Engine: Value Type 4 Bytes, Scan Type Exact Value, type the number, First Scan.
steps.expect: A long list of addresses on the left.

steps.title: Narrow it down
steps.text: Change the number in the game, type the new number, Next Scan; repeat until a handful of addresses remain. Nothing left? The game may keep it as a Float or Double: New Scan with that Value Type, or Unknown initial value, then Increased value / Decreased value.
steps.expect: A few addresses whose value follows the game.

steps.title: Change or freeze it
steps.text: Double-click an address to move it to the address list at the bottom. Double-click its Value to type a new one; tick its Active box to freeze it.
steps.expect: The game shows the new value.

steps.title: Find what writes it
steps.text: Context menu on the address in the list, Find out what writes to this address; accept attaching the debugger, then change the value in the game. The instructions that wrote it appear in the window. That instruction's address is what a lasting patch changes (the x64dbg workbook, or a ViWo patch set).
steps.expect: One or more instructions with their addresses and counts.

steps.title: Save your table
steps.text: File, Save. ViWo's table sits in the workspace (.runtime/cheatengine-gui/<target>/), so your finds travel with the workspace.
steps.expect: The table's file name in the title bar.
